title: When to progress forward with evolving rep ranges
summary: NH explains when to add weight within an evolving rep range: not when every set hits the top of the range, but once a natural rep drop-off shows you can repeat the effort with more weight. He illustrates this with his own squat progression (8-6-4 before adding 10 lb) and says a failed transition means the programming was wrong.
claims: Waiting to hit the top of the range on every set before adding weight turns an evolving rep range back into a static one (4x8-12 becomes 4x12 with a transition period)
The top of an evolving range is a ceiling you don't exceed, not a target to repeat on every set
Reps should drop across sets; two sets with equal reps is fine, but matching reps on three sets means you messed up
With 6-10 for 4 sets, 10-10-10-10 means you should have added weight long ago and 10-10-9-9 a week or two ago, while something like 10-9-8-7 means you are ready
The only way to know which rep pattern predicts success at the next weight is to program it and test it in the gym
His squat progression runs 4, then 5-4, 6-5-4, 7-5-3 and 8-6-4; at 8-6-4 he adds 10 lb and goes back to 4 reps
For him 6-5-4 (15 total reps) does not show readiness for +10 lb; he needs 8-6-4 (18 total)
Add weight once you have shown you can repeat the effort, fight muscular failure and return to baseline within the range
If after a jump you fall below the range's threshold (e.g. 6-5-4 in a 6-10 range), the transition failed and your calculations or recovery were off
If transitions fail around 40% of the time, go back to the drawing board; every transition should be smooth
He has never failed a transition on squats or deadlifts; he failed some on upper body lifts because his jumps were too big, so he reduced them
Strength lifts like squat, deadlift and bench can also evolve the number of sets (e.g. 1 to 3), while accessories can stay at a strict 4 sets of 8-12
Low-rep strength work produces less tonnage than accessories and variations, which should make up the bulk of volume
training_log: 8-6-4 reps across sets, then +10 lb and back to 4 reps
